decisions.rationale: Leading Raichu and Farigiraf denies opposing priority with Armor Tail while providing Fake Out pressure, 4x Psychic coverage into Sneasler, and 100% accurate Mega Raichu Zap Cannon into Blastoise or Delphox. Staraptor and Kingambit in the back punish Incineroar Intimidate with Contrary and Defiant while covering Sinistcha, Delphox, and enemy Kingambit.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Opponent team has Sneasler, Kingambit, Incineroar, Mega Blastoise, Sinistcha, Mega Delphox. Brought Raichu, Farigiraf, Staraptor, Kingambit.

decisions.rationale: Lead Sneasler+Incineroar: double Fake Out pressure plus Intimidate blunts their physical core (Arcanine-H, Staraptor, Kingambit), and Sneasler's 189 Speed with CC/Poison Jab threatens Arcanine (2x), their Kingambit (4x), and Sylveon (OHKO). Quick Guard also answers Raichu Fake Out / Arcanine E-Speed leads. Backline Kingambit+Delphox: Kingambit's Defiant punishes Staraptor's Intimidate, Kowtow Cleave OHKOs Sylveon/Farigiraf, and Sucker Punch pressures frail Mega Raichu-Y; Delphox is my Mega choice (Levitate, 169-204 Speed), resists Pixilate Hyper Voice, and Heat Wave 2x hits their Kingambit. Blastoise is left out because Mega Raichu-Y's No Guard Zap Cannon OHKOs it, and Sinistcha is left out because it's weak to three of their likely four (Staraptor Dual Wingbeat, Arcanine Flare Blitz, Kingambit Kowtow).
decisions.notebook: Opponent team (VR Aug Challenge top-8 list): Raichu (RaichuniteY, LightningRod->No Guard on Mega, Timid 165-200 Spe as Mega; Zap Cannon 100% para, OHKOs my Blastoise, ~80% to Delphox), Arcanine-H (Focus Sash, Rock Head, Jolly; Head Smash/Flare Blitz/E-Speed), Staraptor (Staraptite, Intimidate->Contrary on Mega, Fighting/Flying; CC boosts its defenses), Farigiraf (Sitrus, Armor Tail blocks my Fake Out/Sucker Punch/E-Speed; Trick Room), Sylveon (Fairy Feather Pixilate Hyper Voice; dies to Sneasler Poison Jab and my Kingambit Kowtow), Kingambit (Life Orb Defiant Adamant, 70-102 Spe). Key lines: my Sneasler CC 4x OHKOs their Kingambit; NEVER let Farigiraf Psychic hit Sneasler (4x); my Kingambit is 4x weak to Staraptor CC but gains +2 from its pre-Mega Intimidate (Defiant) and +2 LO Sucker Punch OHKOs Staraptor; do NOT Intimidate Mega Staraptor (Contrary gives +1 Atk); under Trick Room my Kingambit (71 Spe) outslows their Sylveon/Farigiraf (80-112) but their Kingambit may be 70. Sinistcha resists Electric and is immune to Fake Out/E-Speed/CC - Rage Powder can absorb Zap Cannon if brought later. Game 1 plan: Sneasler+Incineroar lead, Kingambit+Delphox back, Mega Delphox.

decisions.rationale: Raichu Mega Evolves into Raichu-Mega-Y to gain No Guard and outspeed Sneasler with 200 raw Speed. Armor Tail blocks any opposing Fake Out attempts. Zap Cannon hits Sneasler with 100% accuracy, breaking its Focus Sash and inflicting guaranteed paralysis, allowing Farigiraf's Psychic to cleanly KO Sneasler on Turn 1 before it can pose a long-term threat.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Opponent brought Sneasler + Incineroar. Raichu Mega Y Zap Cannon + Farigiraf Psychic into Sneasler turn 1.

decisions.rationale: Send in Staraptor to replace fainted Raichu-Mega-Y. Staraptor provides immediate high Speed (167), pre-Mega Intimidate on entry, and massive offensive pressure with Mega Staraptor's Contrary Close Combat against Incineroar and potential incoming dark/steel threats like Kingambit.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Opponent brought Sneasler + Incineroar (Sneasler fainted T1). Raichu fainted T1. Staraptor sent in T2.

decisions.rationale: Double the Raichu slot to secure its KO turn 1: if Raichu Fake Outs either of my Pokémon, the other's attack still lands (Sneasler CC OHKOs; Incineroar STAB Flare Blitz also KOs Raichu's frail 60/55 bulk), and it covers a full-paralysis whiff too. Removing Raichu before it Mega Evolves denies No Guard 100%-paralysis Zap Cannon spam that threatens my whole backline. My Fake Outs are dead into Farigiraf's Armor Tail, so attacking is the only use of Sneasler. Farigiraf's likely Psychic just burns Sneasler's Focus Sash (Incineroar is outright immune), and turn 2 Sneasler outspeeds and OHKOs Farigiraf with 2x STAB Close Combat, with Incineroar Throat Chop as backup. If Raichu Protects or switches, my double still heavily punishes most switch-ins (CC 4x OHKOs their Kingambit, 2x into Arcanine-H through Sash with Flare Blitz cleanup).

Delphox does that best: it outspeeds everything they have left except possibly Mega Staraptor (which Mega Delphox at ~194+ Spe still outspeeds), 2x SE Heat Wave answers their Kingambit (my own Kingambit can't break the mirror at 0.25x), resists Staraptor's Close Combat, and outspeeds Sylveon/Arcanine-H. decisions.rationale: Farigiraf's Armor Tail blocks Incineroar's Fake Out, guaranteeing Trick Room setup while Staraptor lands a heavy Close Combat into Incineroar (which lacks Protect). Under Trick Room, our low Speed control with Farigiraf (80) and benched Kingambit (71) secures a dominant position against Delphox and the remaining opposing roster.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Opponent brought Sneasler + Incineroar + Delphox + 1. Sneasler fainted T1. Incineroar revealed Flare Blitz, ThroatChop, PartingShot, FakeOut (no Protect). Farigiraf set TR T2.

decisions.rationale: Mega Delphox (~204 Spe) outspeeds even Mega Staraptor (max 178) and Psyshock is 2x SE into Mega Staraptor (Fighting), KOing it before it can move; if Staraptor stays non-Mega, its CC only does ~45-65% to Incineroar (survives, Sitrus) and Psyshock+next-turn Psyshock still removes it. This safely absorbs all incoming attacks from Incineroar and Delphox-Mega without taking damage, scouting the opponent's targeting choices while preserving 3 turns of Trick Room for Kingambit to sweep.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Opponent brought Sneasler + Incineroar + Delphox-Mega + 1. Sneasler fainted T1. Incineroar revealed Flare Blitz, Throat Chop, Parting Shot, Fake Out (no Protect). Delphox-Mega revealed Protect, Heat Wave, Psyshock, Nasty Plot. Farigiraf set TR T2.

decisions.rationale: Trick Room makes Incineroar (88) move before Staraptor (132-167), and the estimator confirms -1 Flare Blitz is a guaranteed KO on the 36% Staraptor before it can ever attack (opponent already spent their Mega on Raichu, so no Mega Staraptor/Contrary this game). With the kill locked by Incineroar alone, Delphox doesn't need Psyshock insurance — which would fail vs Protect and is immune into a possible Kingambit switch. Heat Wave instead: if Staraptor faints first it hits Farigiraf at full power (~37-70%, possible KO from 56%), it still chips Farigiraf through a Staraptor Protect, and it punishes any switch-in (2x vs their Kingambit). Farigiraf cannot hurt Incineroar (Psychic immune) and barely dents Delphox (resisted), so this turn is safe and likely ends with Staraptor gone and Farigiraf near KO range for next turn.

Switching Staraptor out to Kingambit brings in our primary Trick Room sweeper safely while Armor Tail protects against priority moves. Under Trick Room, Staraptor (Speed 167) moves before Delphox-Mega (Speed 169–204) to target Incineroar with Close Combat, giving a high chance to KO or severely weaken Incineroar while preserving Farigiraf for Turn 6.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 context: Opponent's Delphox-Mega moveset is Protect, Heat Wave, Psyshock, Nasty Plot. Incineroar moveset is Flare Blitz, Throat Chop, Parting Shot, Fake Out (Sitrus consumed). Sneasler fainted (Focus Sash). Trick Room ends after Turn 6.

decisions.rationale: It's 3v2 with their Kingambit already dead, so no switch-ins remain and no Mega threat (Raichu used their Mega). Psyshock is a guaranteed KO on 36% Staraptor (40.6-78.8%, 100% acc) — only Protect stops it, and even then I lose nothing: Delphox hard-walls Staraptor (CC resisted, Psychic chip only), and once Staraptor falls my Kingambit is outright immune to Farigiraf's Psychic and moves first under their own Trick Room. Doubling Flare Blitz into Staraptor (19.3-38.1%) is unreliable and the recoil only helps Staraptor's CC finish Incineroar, whose survival isn't needed anyway. Throat Chop into Farigiraf (22-43.1%) is free chip with a high-roll KO chance plus end-of-turn burn, and it can't be wasted by a Staraptor Protect.

decisions.rationale: Farigiraf is our last remaining Pokémon at 36% HP against two opponents (Delphox-Mega at 84% and Incineroar at 9%). Since Psychic cannot KO Delphox-Mega from 84% and is immune against Incineroar, Game 1 is lost. Targeting Delphox-Mega with Psychic resolves the turn to transition to Game 2.

decisions.rationale: Farigiraf is their last Pokémon; doubling into it ends the game. Psyshock (17.2-32.3%) + Throat Chop (22-43.1%) have a combined minimum of 39.2% > its 36% HP, so the KO is guaranteed unless Protect succeeds (only 1/3 after last turn's Protect). Both moves are 100% accurate, unlike Heat Wave (90%). Psyshock alone can't KO, so I skip Heat Wave's miss risk. Farigiraf cannot threaten anyone: Psychic is immune into Incineroar/Kingambit and resisted by Delphox at 84%, Helping Hand is useless solo, and a Trick Room reset changes nothing since it has no damage. Even if Protect succeeds, burn chip plus next-turn attacks with TR expired (Delphox 204 outspeeds) close it out risk-free. No Flare Blitz recoil on 10% Incineroar.

reflections.adjustment: Lead Staraptor alongside Farigiraf and save the Mega evolution for Staraptor to utilize Intimidate and immediate Close Combat/Dual Wingbeat pressure against Incineroar and Sneasler.

reflections.summary: Won on team-preview plan plus the turn-1 trade: Focus Sash Sneasler ate Zap Cannon (paralyzed but alive) and, with Incineroar's Flare Blitz, KO'd their Mega Raichu before it got any value. After that their remaining core couldn't break mine — Farigiraf's only attack (Psychic) is immune to Incineroar/Kingambit and barely dents Mega Delphox, Staraptor burned itself trading into Incineroar and fell to even a -2 Psyshock, and their Kingambit died to Flare Blitz chip + Heat Wave. Their own Trick Room favored my slower attackers. The four brought (Sneasler/Incineroar/Delphox/Kingambit) with Mega Delphox suited this opponent perfectly; piloting was clean (0 errors), with only a harmless wasted turn into their double Protect.
reflections.adjustment: Expect a game-2 adaptation since Mega Raichu gave them nothing: most likely Mega Staraptor (Contrary — each Close Combat then raises its defenses, so don't lean on Psyshock) or a Sylveon/Arcanine-H swap. reflections.notebook: Opponent VR Aug top-8 list; ONE Mega per game. Durable strategic facts: Farigiraf is their TR setter with Armor Tail (nullifies ALL my priority — Fake Out/Sucker Punch/Quick Attack/E-Speed — into their side while alive) and its ONLY attack is Psychic, so Incineroar and Kingambit are immune and Mega Delphox takes only ~17% per Psychic — Farigiraf alone can never beat my core; it Protect-stalls (double Protect) to burn TR turns. Staraptor is their only real sweeper: non-Mega Jolly CC takes ~50% off Impish Incineroar per hit; my Delphox Psyshock KOs it even at -2 once chipped; keep my Kingambit far from CC (4x weak). If they Mega Staraptor, Contrary converts CC drops into Def/SpD boosts — kill Farigiraf first, finish with Sucker Punch instead of Psyshock. Their Kingambit falls to Flare Blitz chip + Heat Wave even with Delphox at -1/-2; never Psyshock into a possible Kingambit switch (Dark immune). Raichu's No Guard Mega-Y Zap Cannon auto-paralyzes but Focus Sash Sneasler CC + Incineroar Flare Blitz trades it out turn 1. Game 1 they Mega'd Raichu and benched Sylveon + Arcanine-H — expect a change: vs Sylveon (Pixilate Hyper Voice under TR) Kingambit resists and Kowtow Cleaves super effectively, keep Sneasler away (4x weak); vs Arcanine-H (Focus Sash) my Kingambit resists Head Smash and Delphox Heat Wave is only 0.25x, so use Incineroar/Sneasler CC. My game-1 bring and Mega Delphox choice worked — repeat it, and don't fear their Trick Room, it speeds up my slow attackers.
